hero.title: About AC-Commerce
hero.subtitle: Your complete HVAC marketplace — from first measurement to final sign-off.

intro.p1Rest: is an HVAC marketplace that combines product commerce with professional-grade planning tools. Whether you're buying a mini-split, designing a VRF system for a multi-room property, or getting a certified engineer to review your floor plan — everything happens in one platform.
intro.p2: We replace the fragmented process of juggling multiple vendors, contractors, and design consultants with a single, integrated workflow — from first measurement to final sign-off.

steps.title: Upload Your Floor Plan
steps.text: Upload any architectural PDF/JPG file — residential suite, office, or commercial space. The plan is rendered directly in the browser at high resolution.

steps.title: Mark AC Placements
steps.text: Place labelled AC unit air conditioner symbols on the plan - add comments (ac-1, ac-2...etc) and condenser (outdoor unit air conditioner symbol) placement. Save your work on the cloud.

steps.title: AI-Engineer Review
steps.text: After making an order submission, a certified AI-HVAC engineer opens your submitted plan, adds professional VRF refrigerant lines, and signs off with a digital signature — producing a verified 2-page review PDF. Supports Standard, VRF-Ducted, and VRF-Ductless system configurations. Symbols of ducted HVAC elements/accessories for both ducted and ductless VRF modes — coming soon

steps.title: Save & Download
steps.text: Download your completed AI-engineer-reviewed plan as a PDF with all ac air conditioner symbols, outdoor unit -condenser air conditioner symbol, comments, system lines, and the AI-engineer's digital stamp baked in.

steps.title: BTU Calculator
steps.text: Answer guided questions about your property — room size, insulation, climate — and receive a recommended BTU rating along with a curated list of matching indoor units and outdoor condensers.

steps.title: Recommendations - HVAC System Quote
steps.text: After completing the BTU calculation, review room-by-room HVAC recommendations with matched products, system totals, pricing, print-ready quote output, and quick add-to-cart actions.

features.title: Complete HVAC Marketplace
features.text: Hundreds of mini-split ACs, VRF condensers, indoor units, and accessories from leading manufacturers — with ratings, dimensions, energy ratings, and discounts.

features.title: Professional Notation Tools

hero.title: Advanced Air Conditioning 2026
hero.subtitle: Discover the latest HVAC technologies for comfort, efficiency, and sustainability

advancedAc.intro: 2026 is reshaping home comfort in exciting ways. Today's HVAC systems do far more than heat and cool - they learn your habits, reduce power bills, and create cleaner indoor air for your family. From AI-driven controls to high-efficiency heat recovery and low-impact refrigerants, modern solutions are smarter, quieter, and built for long-term savings. If you're planning an upgrade, this is the perfect moment to discover what next-generation HVAC can do for your home.

heatPumps.title: Heat Pumps: The All-Weather Solution
heatPumps.text: Heat pumps are becoming a go-to solution for homeowners seeking year-round comfort and energy efficiency. With advancements in cold-climate heat pump technology, these systems can now effectively operate in extreme temperatures, making them a versatile choice for any region.

heatRecovery.title: Heat Recovery Systems: Maximize Energy Savings
heatRecovery.p1: Heat Recovery Ventilation (HRV) and Energy Recovery Ventilation (ERV) systems represent a major breakthrough in home energy management. These advanced systems capture and recycle heated or cooled air that would otherwise be lost during ventilation, significantly reducing energy waste and lowering utility bills. Whether you're heating in winter or cooling in summer, heat recovery systems maintain comfort while conserving energy.
heatRecovery.p2: In 2026, HRV and ERV systems are increasingly integrated with smart HVAC solutions, allowing homeowners to optimize airflow based on real-time indoor conditions. The technology works by extracting stale air from your home and transferring its thermal energy to fresh incoming air, effectively reducing the heating or cooling load on your main system. This synergy between heat recovery and climate control can deliver energy savings of 15%–25% annually.
heatRecovery.p3: Leading manufacturers now offer comprehensive heat recovery solutions. Samsung, LG, Daikin, Mitsubishi, Fujitsu, and Panasonic all deliver advanced HRV/ERV systems integrated with their premium AC and heat pump units. Samsung's latest models combine heat recovery with WindFree technology for draft-free cooling, while LG pairs ERV systems with AI-powered energy optimization. Daikin offers modular units that retrofit into existing systems, and Mitsubishi and Fujitsu provide industry-leading VRF-integrated solutions. These compact, whisper-quiet systems are ideal for modern homes seeking premium indoor air quality without sacrificing energy efficiency.

energyEfficiency.title: Energy-Efficient Systems: Saving More, Consuming Less
energyEfficiency.text: Energy efficiency is a leading trend in 2026 HVAC. Modern systems utilize innovations like variable-speed compressors and advanced sensors to maximize comfort while minimizing energy consumption and environmental impact. In 2026, energy efficiency is a key focus in HVAC. New systems employ technologies such as variable-speed compressors and improved heat exchangers to deliver optimal comfort with lower energy use and a smaller carbon footprint.
energyEfficiency.samsungText: The latest collection of air conditioners features Samsung's WindFree Cooling technology, which disperses air through 23,000 micro holes to eliminate direct drafts. Additionally, the AI Fast & Comfort Cooling function enables quick cooling before transitioning to an energy-efficient mode. The AI Energy Mode is designed to optimize cooling settings, potentially reducing energy consumption by up to 30%.

indoorAirQuality.title: Indoor Air Quality Innovations
indoorAirQuality.p1: Improving indoor air quality (IAQ) is a top priority for 2026. HVAC systems are now integrating air purifiers, UV-C light technology, and high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters to remove allergens, bacteria, and viruses from your home's air. These systems ensure a healthier living environment for you and your family.
indoorAirQuality.daikinText: Daikin's new range of Air Purifiers with Streamer Technology are designed to capture, suppress and break down pollutants such as mould, pollen, allergens, odours, formaldehyde, traffic pollution and dust. Perfect for allergy sufferers!

whyUpgrade.title: Why Upgrade in 2026?
whyUpgrade.text: 2026 marks a pivotal year for HVAC upgrades, driven by transformative industry changes. Regulatory mandates now require eco-friendly A2L refrigerants, while new efficiency standards ensure dramatically reduced energy consumption. Modern systems deliver 20%–40% energy savings compared to older models, while advanced smart controls provide unprecedented comfort and convenience. Beyond cost savings, today's units excel in indoor air quality, operate more quietly, and offer precision temperature control. This convergence of environmental responsibility, cutting-edge technology, and substantial long-term savings makes upgrading your HVAC system a smart investment for any home.

costPayback.title: Typical Upgrade Cost and Payback
costPayback.intro: The right system depends on your property size, insulation quality, and usage habits. The guide below gives homeowners a practical starting point before requesting a formal quote.
costPayback.note: Figures are indicative only and can vary by climate, electricity tariff, home envelope performance, and installer scope.

checklist.title: Before You Upgrade: Quick Checklist
items: Confirm room-by-room load sizing, not just whole-home estimates.
Check electrical panel capacity and dedicated circuit requirements.
Review duct condition or ductless layout suitability for your floor plan.
Assess insulation, glazing, and air leakage to avoid oversized equipment.
Verify local rebate, tax incentive, and compliance eligibility before purchase.
Compare installer warranty terms, service response times, and maintenance plans.

designerItems: 📤 Upload PDF/JPG: Select and upload a floor plan PDF/JPG file (accepts .pdf/.jpg only)
↶ Left / ↷ Right: Rotate the PDF/JPG drawing counter-clockwise or clockwise by 90° steps
Reset (°): Appears only when PDF/JPG is rotated — resets back to original 0° orientation
🔍 + / 🔍 −: Zoom in or out on the PDF/JPG canvas (range: 100%–400%)
100% (zoom%): Shows current zoom level; click to reset zoom back to 100%

Notation label input: Text field above the canvas where you type the symbol label before clicking the canvas. The label is reused for each subsequent click — update it any time to change what the next placement will be called.
  • Single-flat AC: ac-1, ac-2, ac-3 …
  • Multi-flat AC (recommended for multi-apartment PDF/JPG files): ac-N.M where N = flat number and M = unit index inside that flat. Example for two flats with three indoor units each: ac-1.1, ac-1.2, ac-1.3 in flat 1 and ac-2.1, ac-2.2, ac-2.3 in flat 2. The Auto-Place HVAC tool groups equipment per flat using this prefix.
  • Condenser: condenser (single flat) or condenser-1, condenser-2 (one per flat in multi-flat drawings).
  • If the input is empty, clicking the canvas places nothing.
Click on canvas: Places an AC / condenser symbol at that position using the current text in the Notation label input. If the input is empty nothing is placed.

🏢 Multi-flat workflow: For PDF/JPG files that contain two or more apartments on one drawing, always use the ac-N.M format so the BTU Calculator, Engineer View auto-placement, and thermostat labels (T1.1, T1.2 …) can separate equipment per flat. Use the matching condenser-N label per flat so each flat gets its own outdoor unit.

📌 Place mode (mobile only): Appears below the toolbar on small screens when a PDF/JPG is loaded. Type the label in the mobile input, then tap 📌 Place mode to activate (turns blue and shows "✅ Tap to place"); only while active can you tap the canvas to place symbols. This prevents accidental placements while scrolling on touch screens.
Drag air conditioner symbol: Click and drag (desktop) or touch and drag (mobile) to reposition an AC symbol
Click air conditioner symbol (desktop): Rotates the air conditioner symbol 90° in place

📌 Placed notations panel: A list of every placed label appears below the canvas as pill-shaped chips (e.g. ac-1 ✏️ 🗑️). The header shows the total count — "📌 Placed notations (n)". Use the chip buttons to edit or delete any notation without hunting for it on the canvas.
✏️ Edit label: Click the pencil icon on the notation chip (works on desktop and mobile) or double-click the label directly on the canvas — a modal opens to rename it.

🗑️ Delete air conditioner symbol: Click the trash icon on the notation chip in the Placed notations panel (works on desktop and mobile). On desktop you can also right-click the air conditioner symbol on the canvas.
Export to BTU (n rooms): Sends all extracted rooms to the BTU Calculator; disabled when no rooms are available
Save: Saves the PDF/JPG with all AC symbols to the backend (shows "Saving..." while in progress)
Clear: Removes all AC symbols, resets the canvas, and clears all session data

btuTab.understandingIntro: BTU (British Thermal Unit) is a measure of heat. This calculator provides an estimation based on common factors:
understandingItems: Base Calculation: 600 BTU/m² used as a base rule.
Outdoor Unit (Condenser) Location: Desired location of outdoor unit.
Number of People: Each person adds ~600 BTU.
Wall Type: Materials and thickness affect BTU.
Insulation Quality: Poor insulation increases BTU needs.
Sun Exposure: More windows or south/west-facing rooms need more cooling.
Window Type: Single-glazed windows allow more heat than triple-glazed.
Apartment Orientation: South and west orientations receive more sunlight.
Floor Type: Materials like marble or tile can retain or reflect heat differently.
Roof Type: Flat roofs may increase heat load compared to pitched or insulated ones.
Appliances: Kitchen and electronic devices contribute additional heat load.
Climate Zone: BTU needs vary by temperature and humidity region.
btuTab.importantNote: Important: This is a general estimate. Consult a licensed HVAC expert for precise system sizing.
